title: Count the Islands
prompt:
You are given a rectangular grid as a slice of string rows, where '#' is land and '.' is water. An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). Return the number of islands. The grid may be empty (no rows, or rows of length 0).

Signature: `fn count_islands(grid: &[&str]) -> usize`

The input is borrowed immutably, so track visited cells yourself. Grids can be large (300 x 300 of solid land), so prefer an explicit stack or queue over deep recursion.

Example:
  count_islands(&[
      "##..#",
      "#...#",
      "..#..",
      "....#",
  ]) -> 4
